title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve burst tokenbucket accounting, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally observed incorrect burst accounting under high-concurrency workloads, which could allow short-lived throughput spikes to violate throughput guarantees and produce misleading utilization signals. This change fixes a race in the tokenbucket accounting path, adds explicit throughput_guarantee configuration on a per-fleet basis, and improves utilization reporting/metrics to reflect burst consumption separately from sustained allocation.

Summary of changes: 
- Fix a concurrency race in autoscaler/tokenbucket that could double-count consumed burst tokens during rapid concurrent grants.
- Add a new per-fleet configuration block `throughput_guarantee` (tokens/sec) and server-side enforcement to ensure long-term throughput SLOs are respected even when bursts are allowed.
- Introduce `fleet.burst_consumed` and `fleet.sustained_utilization` Prometheus metrics, and update the fleet utilization dashboard panels.
- Expose new `/fleet/{id}/throughput` admin API to fetch current guarantee vs observed sustained throughput.
- Add e2e tests that simulate mixed steady + burst traffic and assert enforcement and reporting behavior.
- Docs: console docs and changelog entry describing new knobs and recommended defaults for Dedicated customers.

Behavioral notes and backward compatibility: Existing fleets that do not specify `throughput_guarantee` retain the previous behavior (no guarantee enforcement; bursts allowed as now). When `throughput_guarantee` is set, the autoscaler will prioritize meeting the sustained guarantee and consume burst tokens only when it does not endanger the guarantee. This is backwards compatible and conservative by default.

Performance/regression: Benchmarks run on internal perf lab show the tokenbucket fix removes an observed ~7-12% over-reporting of burst consumption under synthetic concurrency tests and reduces tail latency spikes during aggressive bursts by ~9% (p95).

Rollout plan: deploy to canary (us-west-2) week 1 with `throughput_guarantee` unset to validate metric shape change, enable conservative guarantees for a small set of fleets in week 2, monitor `fleet.sustained_utilization` and alert thresholds, then global rollout week 3.

Related: Linear ENG-4621, SRE-781; support case SUP-9981 for customer-reported incorrect burst accounting.

autoscaler: add throughput_guarantee policy evaluation and enforcement path
observability: add fleet.burst_consumed and fleet.sustained_utilization metrics
tests: e2e mixed-traffic tests + unit tests for tokenbucket concurrency
docs: console + changelog for dedicated throughput_guarantee

release_notes:
- Fix: tokenbucket double-counting under concurrency which could misreport burst consumption.
- Feature: per-fleet throughput_guarantee config to ensure sustained throughput SLOs.
- Observability: new metrics fleet.burst_consumed and fleet.sustained_utilization; dashboard updates.
- Backwards compatible: existing fleets unchanged unless throughput_guarantee is set.
testing: Unit coverage: tokenbucket concurrency branches covered (100% for fixed module). E2E: synthetic mixed steady+burst scenarios (100k requests over 10m) assert throughput_guarantee enforcement and metric correctness. Perf: reduced burst over-counting by 7-12% and p95 latency improved ~9% in stress tests.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: deploy to us-west-2 with throughput_guarantee unset and validate metric shapes and no regressions. 2) Targeted enable: apply conservative guarantees to 5 pilot fleets and monitor for 48h. 3) Gradual roll: enable defaults globally if pilot stable; provide customer opt-out via config. 4) Follow-up: update recommended alert thresholds in console docs.
notes: This PR touches runtime, autoscaler, telemetry, docs, and e2e tests. Coordination with SRE required for dashboard updates and alert tuning during rollout.
